edges.description: A subset of coding or regulatory variants can reduce transcript abundance, protein stability, or another MeCP2 function; the direction cannot be assumed for an untested variant.
edges.source: Function-Altering MECP2 Coding or Cis-Regulatory Variation

edges.description: Altered MeCP2 abundance or function can perturb its transcriptional-regulatory activity.
Model systems suggest that transcriptional dysregulation perturbs synaptic maturation and inhibitory-neuron function.
edges.target: Altered Synaptic and GABAergic Neuron Function

edges.description: The model-system circuit phenotype is hypothesized to contribute to autistic behavior in carriers of function-altering MECP2 alleles.
edges.source: Altered Synaptic and GABAergic Neuron Function

edges.target: Function-Altering MECP2 Coding or Cis-Regulatory Variation

nodes.description: Conditional Mecp2 deletion in mouse GABA-releasing neurons reduces inhibitory signaling and produces repetitive and other Rett/autism-like behaviors. This establishes a plausible circuit route for major MeCP2 loss, not a demonstrated human AUTSX3 mechanism for hypomorphic alleles.
nodes.id: Altered Synaptic and GABAergic Neuron Function

evidence.reference_title: Dysfunction in GABA signalling mediates autism-like stereotypies and Rett syndrome phenotypes.
evidence.snippet: These data demonstrate that MeCP2 is critical for normal function of GABA-releasing neurons and that subtle dysfunction of GABAergic neurons contributes to numerous neuropsychiatric phenotypes.

nodes.description: Autism is the defining phenotype of the susceptibility label. The evidence does not establish an AUTSX3-specific onset, severity distribution, or frequency, and individual MECP2-positive cases may meet criteria for a better-defined MECP2 disorder.

evidence.reference_title: Methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 polymorphisms and vulnerability to autism.
evidence.snippet: This suggests that one or more functional variants of MECP2 existing at significant frequencies in the population may confer increased risk of autism/autism spectrum disorders

evidence.reference_title: MECP2 structural and 3'-UTR variants in schizophrenia, autism and other psychiatric diseases: a possible association with autism.
evidence.snippet: These mutations suggest that a possible association between MECP2 mutations and autism may warrant further study.

nodes.description: MeCP2 binds methylated DNA and participates in both transcriptional repression and activation. Altering MeCP2 activity can therefore change broad neuronal expression programs, but the specific transcriptional program connecting AUTSX3 candidate variants to autism has not been defined in human brain.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptional repression by the methyl-CpG-binding protein MeCP2 involves a histone deacetylase complex.
evidence.snippet: We show that a region of MeCP2 that localizes with the TRD associates with a corepressor complex containing the transcriptional repressor mSin3A and histone deacetylases.

evidence.reference_title: MeCP2, a key contributor to neurological disease, activates and represses transcription.
evidence.snippet: These studies suggest that MeCP2 regulates the expression of a wide range of genes in the hypothalamus and that it can function as both an activator and a repressor of transcription.

nodes.description: The AUTSX3 literature reports heterogeneous candidate alleles: de novo coding variants in autistic females, a segregating p.Gly206Ala missense variant in an autistic male, conserved 3'-UTR variants, and newer noncoding cis-regulatory candidates. Observation in an autistic individual is not by itself proof of causality, and functional effects are variant-specific.
nodes.id: Function-Altering MECP2 Coding or Cis-Regulatory Variation

evidence.reference_title: Identification of MeCP2 mutations in a series of females with autistic disorder.
evidence.snippet: Two autistic disorder females were found to have de novo mutations in the MeCP2 gene.

evidence.reference_title: MECP2 coding sequence and 3'UTR variation in 172 unrelated autistic patients.
evidence.snippet: We report 15 novel variants, not found in controls: one missense, two intronic, and 12 in the 3'UTR (seven in conserved nucleotides).

evidence.reference_title: Sex-aware genome-wide assessment of de novo variants in autism across coding and noncoding regions.
evidence.snippet: three genes that were specific to females, for significance, including TAOK1, MECP2, and DDX3X within a variant class.

evidence.reference_title: MECP2 coding sequence and 3'UTR variation in 172 unrelated autistic patients.
evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that MECP2 can play a role in autism etiology, although very rarely, supporting the notion that MECP2 mutations underlie several neurodevelopmental disorders.

evidence.reference_title: Sex-aware genome-wide assessment of de novo variants in autism across coding and noncoding regions.
evidence.snippet: Direct comparisons of DNVs in males and females revealed MECP2 as the only exome-wide significant gene

evidence.reference_title: Chromosome X-wide common variant association study in autism spectrum disorder.
evidence.snippet: Here, we conducted an X-chromosome-wide association study (XWAS) using whole-genome sequencing data from 6,873 individuals with ASD (82% males) across Autism Speaks MSSNG, Simons Simplex Collection (SSC), and Simons Powering Autism Research (SPARK), alongside 8,981 population controls (43% males).

nodes.description: Functional effects differ by allele. Conserved 3'-UTR changes in four patients were associated with low MECP2 mRNA; a 2026 human-neuron reporter assay found a promoter candidate that reduced expression; and a 2025 yeast/Drosophila screen classified four of nine ASD-catalogued missense variants as loss of function while five retained function.

evidence.reference_title: MECP2 coding sequence and 3'UTR variation in 172 unrelated autistic patients.
evidence.snippet: MECP2 mRNA levels measured in four patients with 3'UTR conserved changes were below the control range, suggesting an alteration in the stability of the transcripts.

evidence.reference_title: A massively parallel reporter assay of MECP2 cis-regulatory elements reveals genetic candidates for male-biased autism.
evidence.snippet: One of these, a promoter variant, disrupts NFY binding and reduces MECP2 expression by ~30%, a magnitude that produces autism-like phenotypes in mice.

evidence.reference_title: Revealing function-altering MECP2 mutations in individuals with autism spectrum disorder using yeast and Drosophila.
evidence.snippet: Our data predict that four ASD variants are loss of function and five are functional.
